question.text: The Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III AIF) has a subscription list with 10 investors. Their commitments (in INR crore) are: 1.0, 1.2, 0.8, 1.5, 0.3 (manager's employee), 2.0 (accredited investor), 0.9, 1.0, 0.25 (manager's employee), 1.1. How many investors BREACH the minimum-investment rule?

explanation.text: The Logic: Rules: INR 1 cr min for non-employee/non-accredited; INR 25 lakh min for employees; AIs have a lower threshold. Check: 1.0 OK; 1.2 OK; 0.8 FAIL (sub-1cr, not employee/AI); 1.5 OK; 0.3 employee (>=25 lakh) OK; 2.0 AI OK; 0.9 FAIL (sub-1cr, not employee/AI); 1.0 OK; 0.25 employee (==25 lakh) OK; 1.1 OK. Two breaches (0.8 and 0.9). The Trap: Trap 1: forgetting that employees have a INR 25 lakh relaxation flags 0.3 and 0.25 as fails (wrong). Trap 2: flagging 2.0 AI as a breach (wrong — AIs have a different threshold). Correct count is 2. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D tests same structure. Manager's Pro-Tip: Auto-flag any commitment < INR 1 cr in your onboarding system and require a tagged exception (employee flag, AI flag) — this catches breaches at KYC stage, not post-allotment.
